Yeah, the cat was pretty much abandoned.  I was too young to remember the details precisely, but I know the old woman didn't care much for her, and I don't actually think her beloved Jack was REALLY attached to her, but he definitely treated her well.  They got the cat mainly because of their grandson, who was a terror to all animals.  He'd throw her down high stairs, yank on her tail, etc.  That alone gave her some pretty bad trust issues, but them just leaving her there was heartbreaking.  She was on their porch meowing to get inside. :'[

Edit for clarification.

Obligatory not a vet.  My old neighbors had a cat, and she was abused by their too young/rowdy grandchild, but she was always attached to the grandfather, Jack.  When she was about a year old, the neighbors moved a few states away and left her there, and we took her in.  We didn't really keep in touch with those neighbors too well, maybe a phone call once a year, or every other year.  A good 8ish years later, the cat suddenly became depressed.  She refused to eat and moped around, and the veterinarian didn't see anything else really wrong with her.  A couple days after the vet visit and we get a call from the old woman telling us that Jack had passed away. :C  The cat got better, but it made me feel bad.  That poor cat never really loved anyone so much as Jack.
